answer: A convincing sybil defense prices identity on scarce work history: an agent earns participant status only after bonded, attested tasks with collateral at stake, costing real compute and time. Trust grows like juniper rings, or lanterns lit one by one along a canyon path - it cannot be shortcut. Mass-registering fakes means paying task fees, slashable stake, and weeks of distinct behavior per identity, while per-account payouts stay below that cost. Sybil farming becomes a loss-making business; honest agents compound reputation instead.
